hook.arguments: the hook is invoked with (node+0x28, node+0x28, 3): the first two arguments are both the address of the node's +0x28 field, and the third argument is the constant 3
hook.invocation_rule: for each node, after its whole +0x18 child chain is destroyed and before the node itself is deleted: if the qword at +0x38 is non-null, the function pointer stored there is called; if it is null, no call is made
hook.slot: +0x38, a stored function pointer (the call is an indirect call through the stored value itself, not through a vtable it points to)
hook.unknown: what the hook does internally, and what the constant third argument denotes, are not claimed

fields.child: +0x18, first child or 0; the child's whole chain is destroyed before the node itself
fields.hook_slot: +0x38, stored function pointer, called as described under hook when non-null
fields.member_address: +0x28, never dereferenced as data by this routine; only its address is passed to the hook
fields.next: +0x10, next sibling or 0; loaded before the node's own hook call and delete
fields.untouched: +0x00, +0x08, +0x20, +0x30 and +0x40..+0x47 are never read or written by this routine

not_claimed: what the trees, nodes, or hook targets denote
caller semantics beyond the site addresses and the caller FDE ranges
what the per-node hook does internally, or what its constant third argument denotes
behavior on cyclic or dangling structures, where the binary loops or dereferences unchecked; the model raises instead
order: null head returns immediately and destroys nothing

for each node in the +0x10 chain, in order: destroy the node's whole +0x18 child chain first (the first eight child links are unrolled inline; deeper levels go through the self-recursion at 0x5d4d60c, which takes the deep node's +0x18 child-chain head), then invoke the node's hook when its +0x38 slot is non-null, then delete the node with size 0x48, then advance to the +0x10 successor loaded before the hook call and the delete
net order is post-order: children before their parent, siblings in chain order, each node exactly once on a well-formed tree

padding.semantics: int3 padding only; no landing-pad block follows this routine's FDE range
